prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures an indoor room about 4 to 6 metres deep where the camera wearer turns slightly right in frames 1 to 3 and then pitches sharply downward toward the carpeted floor in frames 4 and 5. In frames 2 and 3, a sharp bright silhouette marks a person in dark clothing about 1.2 to 1.8 metres away on the left, bent forward facing right and downward away from the camera wearer with floor clutter within their arm's reach, separated by about 1.5 metres of floor from a couch on the right (0.8 to 3 metres away) and a low platform bed 3.5 to 5 metres back near the window. As the camera tilts down in frames 4 and 5, the floor (0.5 to 1.2 metres) and the right-side couch edge (0.5 to 0.8 metres) come within the camera wearer's arm's reach, while the other person is occluded by the left frame boundary except for their lower legs at 1.5 metres in frame 4, and the wearer's own hand enters the bottom-right corner at 0.3 to 0.5 metres in frame 5. Depth reveals the left wall, foreground couch at 0.5 to 1 metre, and overall room geometry in frame 1 despite severe RGB underexposure, and clearly separates the dark-clothed person from dark floor items in frame 2. However, the map is unreliable on small clothes scattered on the floor, clips into over-bright saturation along the right couch cushion in frame 4, and loses background wall and window structure in dark regions.
descriptions.segmentation: Across the five frames, the instance segmentation map attempts to isolate foreground actors and objects as the camera pans from a dark wide view of the room (frames 1 to 3) down toward the floor (frames 4 and 5). In frame 2, it outlines the bent-over person at 1.2 to 1.8 metres on the left—who faces right and looks down at clothes within their arm's reach rather than toward the camera wearer—and in frame 3 it tracks their partially clipped upper body at 1 to 1.5 metres on the lower-left edge as the camera turns toward the couch on the right. While the mask boundary in frame 2 helps separate the dark-clothed person's silhouette from the dark clothing pile beneath their hands, the segmentation map is highly unreliable throughout the sequence and misses key spatial elements like the bed (3.5 to 5 metres away), the floor clutter, the person's legs in frame 4, and the camera wearer's reaching hand at the bottom-right of frame 5 (0.3 to 0.5 metres away). Moreover, it suffers from severe class and boundary hallucinations: in frame 1 it merges the person and room foreground into a single 'person' mask and labels the distant window (4 to 6 metres away) as a 'tv'; in frame 2 it overlays both 'cat' and 'person' labels on the bent person and labels the bright window (4 to 5 metres away) as a 'cup'; and in frames 3 and 5 it misclassifies the close couch on the right (0.8 to 3 metres away, within the wearer's reach) and a floor laundry pile on the left (1 metre away) as 'person' instances.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely blank (all black) across all five frames, failing to register any human keypoints despite people being present in the RGB strip. From the RGB and depth context, another person stands about 1 to 1.8 metres to the left in frames 1 to 3, bent sharply at the waist facing right and looking down at floor items within their arm's reach, before becoming mostly out of view in frame 4 where only their lower legs appear on the left edge at 1.5 metres away. By frame 5, as the camera wearer looks straight down at the floor (0.5 to 1 metre away) next to the right-side couch, the wearer's own right hand enters at the bottom-right edge about 0.3 to 0.5 metres away within arm's reach of the floor, partially clipped by the frame border. Because no yellow body skeletons or magenta hand skeletons are rendered in any frame, this map adds no spatial information over RGB and is entirely unreliable here, failing under the dark lighting of frame 1, the steep self-occluding bend and frame-edge clipping of the other person in frames 2 to 4, and the motion blur and partial view of the wearer's hand in frame 5.
